articles.title: Justin Minaya se convierte en el undécimo fichaje del Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El alero estadounidense, con pasaporte dominicano, de 27 años y 1,96 metros firma por dos temporadas tras una amplia experencia en la G League
articles.summary: El alero estadounidense, con pasaporte dominicano, de 27 años y 1,96 metros firma por dos temporadas tras una amplia experencia en la G League
articles.body: El Barcelona oficializó la llegada del alero Justin Minaya, de 27 años y 1,96 metros. Es el undécimo fichaje de la plantilla azulgrana para esta temporada y firma por dos temporadas. Minaya nació en Nueva Jersey pero posee la nacionalidad dominicana y es internacional con su selección. No ocupará plaza de extracomunitario en las competiciones ACB. Procede de los Osceola Magic, equipo de la G League, con los que el curso pasado promedió 9,8 puntos con un 30,5% en triples, 4,2 rebotes y 2,3 asistencias en 34 encuentros disputados. Formado en la Northern Valley High School, sus primeros pasos en el baloncesto universitario fueron en Carolina del Sur, de la mano de los Gamecocks (2017-21). La última aventura, antes de probar suerte en el draft de la NBA de 2022, fue con los Providence de Rhode Island (2021-22). Inició su andadura hacia la NBA con el único equipo de la G-League que no tiene ningún equipo asociado, los Mexico City Capitanes. Consigue una media de 12,7 puntos, 4,4 rebotes y 2,1 robos por partido. Los Portland Trail Blazers le incorporan a su disciplina, el 4 de abril de 2023. Jugó durante tres temporadas en las que disputó 57 encuentros con promedios de 1,7 puntos y 1,4 rebotes. Las dos últimas, con un contrato dual, que le permite jugar también en la G League. Al acabar la campaña 2023-24, firmó un contrato con los Orlando Magic, pero no llega a debutar. Ahora vivirá su primera aventura en Europa. Su fichaje por el Barcelona, se suma a los de Justin Robinson, Umoja Gibson, Agustín Ubal, Stanley Umude, Tyrese Martin, Olivier Nkamhoua, Tosan Evbuomwan, Josh Nebo, Olek Balcerowski y Yoan Makoundou, además del nuevo entrenador Aleksander Sekulic. Una renovación completa de la plantilla en la que sólo permanecen de la campaña anterior Punter, Darío Brizuela, Joel Parra y Juan Núñez.

articles.title: French trans player Julie Tetart addressed WNBA chatter and Sophie Cunningham’s stance
articles.summary: Amid all the WNBA draft rumours, Julie Tetart has already addressed her chances of playing in America. For anyone who still doesn’t know, Julie Tetart is a 6...
articles.body:
Amid all the WNBA draft rumours, Julie Tetart has already addressed her chances of playing in America.

For anyone who still doesn't know, Julie Tetart is a 6-foot-3 French professional basketball player who identifies as a transgender woman. Before her transition, she spent nearly two decades playing in France's men's regional divisions.

After publicly coming out in 2021, she stepped away from the sport for about three years to undergo her gender transition and multiple surgeries before returning to the court in 2024 with Monaco.

Her dominant stat lines, averaging over 20 points and 20 rebounds per game, placed her directly at the center of the WNBA's ongoing eligibility debate.

However, while viral social media claims recently suggested she declared for the WNBA draft, no official paperwork or announcement exists, it remains pure internet speculation.

Julie Tetart throws doubt over WNBA opportunity

Despite the rumours coming recently of a potential entry into the WNBA draft, Julie Tetart has already spoken about her chances.

Speaking to OutKick over Instagram in direct messages at the start of August, Tetart shared how she would love to play in the WNBA. but she can't see herself in America given the strong policies.

She said: "If they contact me, I won't say no. But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!

"Obviously, it's a childhood dream just like for any female basketball player, but unfortunately, it's not possible. The league, yes. The country, no, haha."

Tetart was then asked about Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham's recent remarks , where she wants to "protect young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

She replied: "Aucun," which translated to English is, "None."

Even with Enes Kanter and Royce White's efforts, it's highly unlikely that the WNBA will allow biological men to play in the league anytime soon.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever React to MVP Race as Star Drops Rare Box-Score Stats Ahead of World Cup Break
articles.summary: After leading the Indiana Fever to 12 wins in 16 games entering the FIBA World Cup hiatus, Caitlin Clark has put herself square in the middle of the MVP race.
articles.body:
After leading the Indiana Fever to 12 wins in 16 games entering the FIBA World Cup hiatus, Caitlin Clark has put herself square in the middle of the MVP race.

On the heels of the Fever's recent victory over the Connecticut Sun, Clark downplayed her individual stats by saying she's not thinking about the box score and the numbers are just a product of the flow of the game.

"I don't really care about the stats," she explained. "When I'm just flowing and playing, that's kinda what follows. That's kinda how I've been over the last couple games. Obviously, you're not gonna have 30-plus [points], 10-plus [assists] every night, but when you're able to do that it just allows the team to get going in a different way. Making shots, getting people open, that's contagious. It's contagious to the team."

Angel Reese breaks yet another WNBA record

Clark became the first player in WNBA history to record back-to-back games with at least 30 points and 10 assists. She had 37 and 10 in the Fever's 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky on Aug. 23.

Even though Clark didn't want to pump herself up, Makayla Thompson was happy to give her teammate flowers.

"I mean, she's incredible," Thompson said. "She's our GOAT in the league. You know what I'm saying? I mean, she just gives it her all every night. She just does all the things that she's going to do. She's shooting the ball well, giving great assists and just being her overall."

Also offering praise for Clark was Fever head coach Stephanie White (starts at 5:25 mark), who explained it can be "easy to take for granted some of the things that she does" on the court:

"It's easy to take advantage and think it's simple, and I think that's why players are great. They make the complex things look really simple. And when she's in a flow like this where she's able to score, she's playing at a pace that we want her to play at. She's moving the ball, getting it side to side, it's really, really fun to watch. Sometimes you can get caught up on the sideline just watching. So, it's really special what she's doing."

Since July 17, Clark is averaging 25.9 points on 49.6 percent shooting (43.1 percent from three) and 9.3 assists per game in 16 starts. She has eight double-doubles and one triple-double during this stretch.

Not coincidentally, the Fever have turned their season around to become a top-tier title contender. They were 14-10 after an 88-75 loss to the Golden State Valkyries on July 15.

The Fever have had two winning streaks of five games since that period. Their 12-4 record since July 17 is tied with the Atlanta Dream for the second-best in the league. They are averaging a WNBA-best 102.7 points per game during this stretch.

Indiana enters the FIBA break in fifth place in the playoff standings, but tied with the Dream at 26-14 overall. Those two clubs are only one game behind the Las Vegas Aces for the No. 3 seed.

The WNBA season resumes on Sept. 17 with every team having four games remaining in the regular season.

Indiana has a difficult closing stretch with games against the Washington Mystics, followed back two games against the Minnesota Lynx in three days from Sept. 22-24.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors on Jalen Duren's Contract Talks With Pistons, Timeline for Potential Resolution
articles.summary: Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are seemingly entering the home stretch of their contract standoff given the Oct. 1 deadline for players to accept the qualifying offer, but it may not be resolved until closer to that date.
articles.body:
Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are seemingly entering the home stretch of their contract standoff given the Oct. 1 deadline for players to accept the qualifying offer, but it may not be resolved until closer to that date.

Per ESPN's Tim MacMahon , one executive from an opposing team explained there remains a "gap" between Duren and the Pistons on a long-term deal.

"There's still a gap," the exec said, "and it's going to drag."

MacMahon noted the Pistons have been willing to offer Duren a five-year deal "in the range" of $35 million per season, but Duren's camp is seeking a contract worth more than $40 million annually.

Duren was one of six members of the 2022 draft class who received a qualifying offer this summer. The others — Mark Williams, Bennedict Mathurin, Tari Eason, Walker Kessler and Peyton Watson — have all signed multiyear deals.

Kessler and Watson left their original team in sign-and-trade deals. It doesn't seem like that's ever been a consideration for the Pistons, who have not shown any interest in trading the 22-year-old.

The qualifying offer would pay Duren $9.6 million for the 2026-27 season. He would also be eligible for unrestricted free agency next summer.

A contract worth in the range of $35 million per season would make Duren the 10th highest-paid center by average annual salary in the NBA, sandwiched between Rudy Gobert ($36.5 million) and Bam Adebayo ($32.6 million).

Adding to the complicated nature of the contract negotiations is the apron, which MacMahon wrote has led the Pistons to take a "relatively tough stance" with Duren.

The Pistons already have Cade Cunningham on a supermax extension . They are also trying to work out a long-term deal with Ausar Thompson, which some projections suggest could range anywhere from $33-40 million per season.

If Thompson and Duren each get roughly $40 million annually, the Pistons are locked in with them and Cunningham as their main trio for the next few years.

Despite coming off a breakout 2025-26 regular season that earned him a spot on the All-NBA third team, Duren hurt his value with a rough playoff showing. He averaged 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds per game in 14 playoff starts, scoring fewer than 10 points in seven of those games.

Duren was much better in the regular season, averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game in 70 starts. He helped keep the Pistons going strong when Cunningham missed three weeks late in the season due to a collapsed lung.

Detroit's 60 wins in the regular season were the most for the franchise since 2005-06.

articles.title: Victor Oladipo Writes Open Letter to NBA GMs Amid Comeback Attempt After 2023 Injury
articles.summary: As he continues to chase a comeback to the NBA, veteran guard Victor Oladipo sent a direct message to general managers across the league.
articles.body:
As he continues to chase a comeback to the NBA, veteran guard Victor Oladipo sent a direct message to general managers across the league.

Oladipo penned an open letter to GMs in The Players' Tribune explaining his motivations to return to the NBA for the first time since 2023.

A two-time All-Star, Oladipo's once-promising career took a hit when he suffered a ruptured quad in 2019. The injury plagued him for years, and after eventually returning to the court, he later suffered a torn patellar tendon in the 2023 playoffs. Since then, he's had stints playing overseas and in the G League, but a team has yet to take a chance on adding him to the main roster.

In his open letter, Oladipo addressed his injury recovery, but he revealed that his primary source of motivation is to play in front of his four-year-old daughter, Naomi, whom he affectionately calls Nomi.

"It's this version, right now, that I want Nomi to see," Oladipo wrote. "Me, in this moment of my life, at 34 years old. The version of her dad that got kicked all the way down the mountain, then spent years trying to climb back up, only to get kicked back down, again and again … but never once quit trying to climb. The version of her dad that, let's be real, is probably getting counted out by a lot of people, and is probably getting laughed at by a few of them … but has managed to keep his faith, and keep his purpose.

"The version of her dad that's finally found the perspective, and the humility, to write a letter like this one. To say to any GM who's willing to listen: I believe my body is finally right. I believe I still have GREAT (and more importantly, WINNING) basketball in front of me. I believe I can be a valuable contributor to an NBA locker room. And what I'm asking for right now is an opportunity to prove it."

Oladipo held an open workout for NBA teams in Las Vegas in July. Last month, he teased that he received "some interest" from the Sacramento Kings following the retirement of veteran guard Russell Westbrook, and he added that "the feeling is mutual."

The NBA preseason is right around the corner before the 2026-27 campaign starts next month, so Oladipo could get his shot to prove himself if a team is willing to take a chance on him in the coming weeks.

articles.title: CaixaBank entrega la camiseta oficial del Mundial a la Selección Femenina de baloncesto
articles.standfirst: Gonzalo Gortázar, consejero delegado de CaixaBank, despidió a la selección femenina le deseó suerte en el Mundial en el que debuta España este viernes
articles.summary: Gonzalo Gortázar, consejero delegado de CaixaBank, despidió a la selección femenina le deseó suerte en el Mundial en el que debuta España este viernes
articles.body: CaixaBank, socio patrocinador de la FEB, ha organizado el último acto oficial de la Selección Española femenina de baloncesto en tierras españolas antes de poner rumbo al Mundial de Alemania 2026. Gonzalo Gortázar, consejero delegado de CaixaBank, ha querido acompañar personalmente al cuerpo técnico y a 11 de las 12 jugadoras convocadas, así como a la Presidenta de la FEB -Elisa Aguilar- para despedirlas antes de la cita mundialista y hacerles entrega de la camiseta oficial con la que disputarán un nuevo Mundial, al que regresan tras ocho años. El encuentro, celebrado en la Terminal 4 del Aeropuerto Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas, se ha desarrollado en una sala habilitada para la ocasión donde Gortázar ha podido hacer entrega de la camiseta con la que disputarán los partidos oficiales. Dicha camiseta incorpora ya el parche oficial de la Federación Internacional de Baloncesto para las Selecciones participantes en el Campeonato del Mundo de Baloncesto Femenino de Alemania 2026. Durante el encuentro, Gonzalo Gortázar, consejero delegado de CaixaBank, ha deseado suerte al equipo y le ha trasladado el apoyo de la entidad ante uno de los grandes retos deportivos de la temporada. “Esta selección representa ambición, talento, trabajo en equipo y capacidad para volver a ilusionar a todo un país. Para CaixaBank es un orgullo acompañaros en este Mundial. Os deseamos el mayor de los éxitos y, sobre todo, que disfrutéis de un camino que ya es un ejemplo para muchas niñas y jóvenes”, ha señalado Gortázar. En el acto ha estado presente Elisa Aguilar, presidenta de la Federación Española de Baloncesto (FEB), quien ha querido destacar que “esta camiseta que hoy recibe el equipo tiene un valor especial, y también un peso muy importante, porque es con la que la Selección asume la representación de España en esta Copa del Mundo. Gracias a CaixaBank y a Gonzalo Gortázar por su apoyo de todos estos años a nuestro baloncesto femenino, y por protagonizar un acto tan simbólico, el momento en que estas jugadoras pasan a ser quienes enarbolan la bandera de nuestro país en un Mundial al que regresamos, cargados de sueños, ocho años después”. La selección afronta la cita bajo el lema ‘Volvemos a soñar’, con el que la FEB ha querido implicar a la afición en el regreso del equipo a un Mundial ocho años después. Berlín 2026 será la octava participación mundialista de España. En las siete anteriores, la selección consiguió tres medallas: bronce en República Checa 2010, plata en Turquía 2014 y bronce en Tenerife 2018. El campeonato supondrá, además, el debut mundialista de una nueva generación: salvo Alba Torrens, ninguna de las jugadoras de la convocatoria definitiva había disputado antes esta competición. También será el primer Mundial de Miguel Méndez como seleccionador nacional. España llega a Berlín como actual subcampeona de Europa tras la medalla de plata obtenida en el Europeo de Atenas 2025. Para este nuevo ciclo, CaixaBank también se ha volcado con su propio eslogan ‘Volvemos a creer’, que destaca el elemento esencial que hay detrás de todo un campeonato de esta envergadura: la emoción. CaixaBank es socio patrocinador de la Federación Española de Baloncesto (FEB) y patrocinador oficial de la selección española, tanto femenina como masculina, en todas sus categorías, que van desde la absoluta hasta la sub-16, y patrocinador principal de la Federación Española de Deportes de Personas con Discapacidad Física, con el objetivo de impulsar el baloncesto en silla de ruedas. Al mismo tiempo, la entidad financiera es patrocinadora de múltiples canteras de baloncesto en España, tanto profesionales como amateurs. A través de la vinculación con los equipos, CaixaBank promueve la práctica y la promoción del baloncesto para equipos de formación y escuelas de baloncesto en todo el territorio de influencia. Mediante estos acuerdos CaixaBank fomenta la participación en competiciones oficiales de dichos equipos, así como la organización de campus, concesiones de becas a jóvenes deportistas y formación de entrenadores. La entidad financiera lleva apoyando al baloncesto nacional desde el año 2013 y su implicación y la activación de múltiples iniciativas en torno a este deporte han ayudado a visibilizar y ampliar la repercusión de los mayores éxitos cosechados internacionalmente. En su implementación de la estrategia de patrocinio local, CaixaBank ha colaborado con los principales eventos baloncestísticos que se han celebrado en la última década en España, tanto profesionales como amateurs, trasladando los valores del deporte a todos los rincones del país. Prueba de ello es la apuesta como patrocinador oficial de la Copa del Mundo de 2014 celebrada en España, la colaboración con la Copa del Mundo de Baloncesto Femenino celebrada en Tenerife el año 2018, el Eurobasket femenino que se disputó en Valencia en 2021. Igualmente, cabe destacar el histórico compromiso con el Circuito 3x3 CaixaBank, el mayor circuito de baloncesto 3x3 en la calle que se disputa desde el año 2012, una de las competiciones de referencia del deporte base que ha congregado a 64.000 jugadores de todas las edades y que ha recibido más de 475.000 visitantes tras realizar 143 paradas en más de 50 ciudades españolas a lo largo de su historia. CaixaBank también colabora con la FEB con el fin de fomentar un programa de voluntariado deportivo que trascendiera la propia competición: el programa voluntarios FEB CaixaBank. Creado con motivo de la Copa del Mundo Masculina celebrada en España 2014, hoy en día, el programa ha conseguido tejer una sólida comunidad de cerca de 25.000 voluntarios, que dan apoyo a todos los eventos oficiales de baloncesto organizados por la FEB.

articles.title: Nvidia's DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Tech Officially Launches on September 3, Hits Performance by Around 50–60%
articles.summary: Just last week, Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 technology leaked when a DLL file was found in the NBA 2K27 beta. It shouldn't be too surprising, then, that the technology will be officially launching on September 3 in, well, NBA 2K27.
articles.body:
Just last week, Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 technology leaked when a DLL file was found in the NBA 2K27 beta. It shouldn't be too surprising, then, that the technology will be officially launching on September 3 in, well, NBA 2K27 .

Nvidia bills DLSS 5 as a 3D-bound neural rendering technique, which takes geometry and color data from the game you're playing, and then draws an AI-generated image on top of the rendered frame. The goal is to maximize photorealism, without the massive computational cost that would require in more traditional methods. Nvidia insists that because the model is constrained by the geometry and color information in the original scene, that it won't add extra elements to the scene or misplace objects. But that's something I'll have to test when the tech becomes available Thursday.

Regardless of the aesthetic changes that DLSS 5 has in games, it doesn't come for free. While some of the mods that materialized after the leak on Friday had some massive performance hits, I assumed that was partly because of a lack of optimization. However, even according to Nvidia, enabling the DLSS 5 neural renderer in NBA 2K27 will hit performance by around 50–60%. Although, it will have a noticeable impact on how the game looks.

To offset that performance hit, Nvidia encourages folks to enable the other parts of the DLSS software suite , like super resolution and frame generation to keep your frame rate high. The technology will also only work on RTX 5000 graphics cards at launch, but I'd recommend only enabling it if you have an RTX 5070 or better.

You can, of course, lower graphics settings or resolution to give yourself more leeway, but according to Nvidia, the better the source, the better the final image is going to look. I'm not sure what minimum graphics settings at a low resolution will do to the final image once DLSS 5 actually launches, but that's definitely something I'm going to test later this week.

Regardless, while DLSS 5 has had a controversial lead up to its release , I've definitely seen plenty of people in my own comments who think it makes games look much better. And now that it's going to be officially supported in a game by its developers we'll finally be able to see it in action beyond Nvidia's own marketing – and I know I'm excited to see exactly what it can do, and where it falls short.

Jackie Thomas is the Hardware and Buying Guides Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: New Warriors Rumors on Stephen Curry Contract Talks, Jaren Jackson Jr. Trade Pursuit
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are reportedly leaving the ball in the court of star point guard Stephen Curry when it comes to contract negotiations.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are reportedly leaving the ball in the court of star point guard Stephen Curry when it comes to contract negotiations.

During Tuesday's episode of The Hoop Collective , ESPN's Anthony Slater provided an update on Curry's expected contract extension and revealed that the Warriors are letting him decide his future with the franchise.

"They're not like negotiating with Steph Curry right now. They are saying, 'You can do this, you can do this, you can do this. If you want the one-year max, if you want the two-year max, if you want to wait, here's your menu. Pick off your menu,'" Slater said (5:24 mark).

Slater also revealed that the Warriors attempted to trade for star center Jaren Jackson Jr. before he was ultimately sent from the Memphis Grizzlies to the Utah Jazz at the deadline this past season.

"I'll give you one that is probably talked about least in the last few years of swings and misses: it's Jaren Jackson at the deadline," Slater said (11:05 mark). "They were kind of sniffing around that."

The 2026-27 season is the final year on Curry's current contract, and he's slated to make a league-high $62.6 million. This past Saturday, he officially became eligible for an extension of up to two years and $136.7 million. The 38-year-old recently told Dalton Johnson of NBC Sports Bay Area that he hopes to finish his career in Golden State.

"There's no question I want to be here the rest of my career, and I'm pretty sure that's going to happen," he said. "... The deal and the contract stuff will happen at the right time, and we're not letting it be a distraction from our preparation for the season, and the fact that the team we're coming back with has a lot of familiarity."

Still, it's safe to say that the Warriors are not expected to contend for an NBA championship this season in the competitive Western Conference. While Golden State has maintained its veteran-laden roster, the team has failed in multiple trade pursuits over the past few years that would've added another star next to Curry.

As Curry nears the end of his legendary career, the Warriors will have to figure out a way to bring more talent to the Bay Area so they can return to title contention before the four-time champion steps away for good.

articles.title: Klay Thompson to Miami, DeMar DeRozan to Denver and the NBA offseason's most underrated moves
articles.summary: Here are six acquisitions that could prove to be sneaky good fits.
articles.body:
As we inch closer and closer to fall (you already took a sip of a Pumpkin Spice something, I know it), we can feel the optimism spreading within the basketball world.

The offseason is full of transactions, moves to improve and swings to make things … fit . That's the key word. Context, opportunity and how a new acquisition works within what a team does will end up defining how well a transaction ends up being.

It's easy to view moves in a vacuum. Teams need to acquire talent to fit a need, talent needs an opportunity to work, etc. But my curiosity always forces me to dig a little deeper: Maybe adding this player did not address every weakness a team has, but how did it make them stronger? What can teams do with these additions that they could not do last year?

So with that in mind, I present to you my six pack of underrated fits with NBA training camps opening later this month.

This is less about Klay Thompson returning to All-Star form, less about Klay being Ray Allen to Miami 2.0, and more about the fit between the human, the player and the franchise. It's clear Thompson wants to compete at a high level, and the Heat are always going to work to compete at a high level, especially after cashing in their chips to get Giannis Antetokounmpo. Erik Spoelstra has a knack for understanding his roster, knowing where his team needs to go and getting the most out of his roster. It feels like a natural meeting of the minds.

It's not hard to imagine how Thompson, one of the greatest 3-point shooters of all time, will help Miami when it comes to spacing. But Thompson is not just a great shooter, he's a movement shooter and a willing shooter. For the Heat, that can open up the playbook. Giannis will always draw the attention of a defense, but Thompson gives them someone who can be used in different actions as a threat when he's off the board. If you don't believe me, wait until the first time Klay makes four-plus 3s in Miami and listen to the crowd.

Many will point to the defensive end of the floor, point to his age and point at me. What I will say in response is, with Andrew Wiggins, Bam Adebayo and Giannis, there is a good amount of size and length that can surround Thompson on defense. Miami and Thompson needed each other, and that should pop throughout the season.

When the Minnesota Timberwolves reshaped the vision for their team by acquiring LaMelo Ball, it felt like the team was upgrading their guard position while also locking themselves into small ball. Being able to add a young, dynamic talent like Jonathan Kuminga to that vision feels like a major plus for Minnesota.

Before I get to the basketball aspects, it's important to note that Minnesota wanted him there. From the top of the organization, to the front office, to the roster and Anthony Edwards, they clearly valued his talent and what he could add to what they are building. How much value does that have for Kuminga, considering his feelings about how things went in Golden State? Forget the fanfare and ink being spilled for a moment, the human nature to feel wanted can unlock a whole lot of things.

On the court, not immediately having to tap Jaden McDaniels at the 4 all the time feels like a big win for the Timberwolves. They can get to some lineup versatility and different combinations. Considering the guard room the Wolves have, there will always be a certain level of talent on the floor. Kuminga's athleticism should immediately be felt in transition. His confidence offensively and ability to self-create should also help Minnesota in moments where the offense has a lull. If there is a boost in catch-and-shoot 3s and driving closeouts, the Wolves become even tougher to guard.

Tim Connelly has had an eye on getting talent in the room and Chris Finch has had a knack for getting the most out of it. We have seen the franchise take a player who may be seen as something, and then seeing something in them. The growth of Julius Randle, the evolution of Naz Reid, the immediate turn from Ayo Dosunmu, the playoff version of McDaniels — all of those leaps came in-house. So it's not hard to imagine that a young player looking for a home and a chance to prove himself pops in an environment that may be the best context he's had.

There has been a lot of conversation about the Denver Nuggets' offseason, and I fully understand where it's coming from. The way they lost their playoff series to the Timberwolves coupled with a lack of a big offseason move and the loss of Peyton Watson may not feel the best to a lot of people. But if we move all of that to the side and I told you a 54-win team with the best offensive rating in the NBA last season added DeMar DeRozan, would it feel so bad?

(It might. I know you're rolling your eyes right now, but stick with me.)

A lot of times additions are viewed in a very specific tunnel. This team is bad at X, and if we don't fix that, we won't get where we want to. I understand that. And I understand if you add a player that you also believe is bad at X, it can ruffle some feathers. My counter would be that sometimes a team may see what it needs but may not be able to find it at the moment. That doesn't stop its pursuit of greatness, it just makes it … a little different.

What if I told you the Nuggets may have worked to strengthen their strength — to add to what they already do very well offensively, even if it's in a way that may not 100% vibe with the sounds of "modern basketball"? One of the best offenses adding one of the best bucket getters is an interesting concept. Make no mistake about it, until the day he hangs up his shoes DeRozan will be a bucket getter. How many of those has Denver had in this era?

If we're being honest, half of what people felt about the growth from Aaron Gordon last season was his ability to go find a basket within the team's context. DeRozan has the ability to provide stability to the Nuggets' second unit without having to relentlessly smash the Jamal Murray button. And for a team that has made life difficult in the fourth quarter for opponents having to figure out how to guard Nikola Jokić, Murray and Gordon, I'm not sure adding DeRozan to the mix makes that easier.

Would this also not be the best offensive context DeRozan has had? And if you're worried about the defense, we can be honest with each other, how many players would have to be added to Denver for you to not be? We have proof of concept: If you can't stop them and they can stop you enough, they will always be hard to deal with.

Isaiah Joe/Kevin Huerter/Gary Harris/Taurean Prince/John Collins to Detroit

Yes, I am aware that as I write this we do not have an ending to the long-term storyline of Jalen Duren and the Pistons. But I also watch soap operas, so I know that a) eventually we'll get a conclusion and b) I can pivot to other people without much concern. So I present the Pistons seeing an Eastern Conference chasing them down, doubling down on their identity, and also saying, "Hey, what if we just have more shooting?"

Bring me Isaiah Joe and his ability to be used in different actions. Kevin Huerter, let's see if you can let it fly. Gary Harris and Taurean Prince, you shot well from deep, come over here and do that. John Collins, you've been working to expand that part of your game, why not?

The percentages and the volume are going to shift and change, but what I like for Detroit is the fact it has options. It can maintain a level of spacing around the continued growth of Cade Cunningham and what I would assume to be the two-man game with him and Duren. If you're going to help, they have different people who can make you pay. And never forget, they are going to guard you . They'll never stop guarding you.

I am an enjoyer of taking a swing on talent, and if you're New Orleans trying to figure out what the next era will be, why not take a swing on Bennedict Mathurin?

He's showcased an ability to score over and over again, he adds a dynamic with his shot creation and driving, and there have been flashes defensively. What is the worst thing that can happen?

It's the Western Conference, so results will always vary, but having a lot of offensive talent may not be the end of the world. Mathurin likely has a desire to prove himself in a different way, and the way he does it may help the Pelicans figure out exactly what they want to do going forward.

This felt like the sneakiest move of the offseason. The Spurs absolutely put the league on notice last year. They will have to deal with going from the hunter to the hunted, but they will also have to figure out how to navigate the effects from losing in the NBA Finals. Where Tobias Harris helps them is not just from being a veteran, but by adding to the foundation they have already laid.

Harris showcased a different level in his ability to score in Detroit; being able to do that in San Antonio with less responsibility should be a plus for both sides. He can also guard multiple positions, space the floor, and be used in different actions. The beauty is that the Spurs won't have to rely on Harris to do those things in theory. And he's coming off a year where defense meant everything in Detroit and he can carry that over with Victor Wembanayama now behind him. If he stays in form, this could open another door for the Spurs.

articles.title: Michigan's Brandon McCoy's Knee Injury Return Timeline Revealed, 5-Star SG Was Top-10 Recruit
articles.summary: The start of the college basketball season is still months away, but Michigan's national championship defense already took a major hit.
articles.body:
The start of the college basketball season is still months away, but Michigan's national championship defense already took a major hit.

The Wolverines announced on Tuesday that freshman shooting guard Brandon McCoy will miss the entire 2026-27 season after suffering a torn ACL. McCoy was a 5-star recruit and the No. 10 overall player in the 2026 class in 247Sports' composite .

Per Clayton Sayfie of On3.com, McCoy injured his knee 20 seconds into an exhibition game against Serbian professional team Mega SUPERBET on Aug. 27 in Croatia when he fell awkwardly while attempting a layup. He had to be carried off the court by teammates, and he didn't return to the bench for the remainder of the game.

Before going down with the injury, McCoy impressed in the first two games of the Wolverines' European trip. Sayfie reported that the youngster recorded 14 points, five rebounds and four steals in his Michigan debut against the Lithuania National Team before finishing with 15 points and five rebounds against the Lithuania National B Team.

A 6'5", 190-pound prospect out of Sierra Canyon High School in California, McCoy has the makings of a future two-way star. 247Sports director of scouting Adam Finkelstein described him as "one of the very best defenders in the class" and "a physically gifted guard who plays with a motor, imposes his will on the game on both ends of the floor, and has room for future growth with the progression of his shooting and total guard skills."

Losing McCoy will certainly hurt Michigan's depth in the backcourt, but the Wolverines should be able to manage his absence with veterans like senior guard Elliot Cadeau leading the way.

articles.title: Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr. Sign 76ers Contracts, Latest NBA Rumors Reveal Details
articles.summary: One of the tallest players in NBA history will audition to join LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers this season.
articles.body:
One of the tallest players in NBA history will audition to join LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers this season.

Tacko Fall has signed with the Sixers ahead of training camp later this month, the team announced Tuesday. The deal is an Exhibit 10 contract, per ESPN's Dave McMenamin .

The 76ers also signed Saint Thomas and Jameer Nelson Jr., son of former NBA All-Star and Sixers EVP of basketball operations Jameer Nelson. These contracts are also Exhibit 10 deals, per McMenamin.

Exhibit 10 contracts, which can be converted into two-way deals, allow teams to bring in players to compete for NBA for G League roster spots on one-year, non-guaranteed contracts, per Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman.

Fall, Nelson and Thomas will participate in Sixers training camp on these deals, according to McMenamin.

NBA teams can hand out two-way contracts to three players each season. The Sixers had a pair of these roster spots remaining after signing Caleb Love, a two-way player for the Portland Trail Blazers last season, earlier this offseason.

After four years with the University of Central Florida, Fall appeared in 26 games with the Boston Celtics and 11 with the Cleveland Cavaliers when playing in the NBA from 2019 to 2022.

The 7-foot-6 big man averaged 2.2 points and 2.4 rebounds per game during that stretch. He played last season for the Chinese Basketball Association's Ningbo Rockets, averaging 11.2 points on 80.1 percent shooting through 38 games.

Nelson, a point guard who closed out his college career with TCU in 2024, spent most of last season with the G League's Stockton Kings. He averaged 19.9 points on 46.5 percent shooting from the field through 11 regular-season games with the team.

His father was promoted to his current role in June after previously serving as assistant general manager and now serves as the franchise's top executive behind president Mike Gansey, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Nelson signed Exhibit 10 contracts with the San Antonio Spurs in 2024 and the Sacramento Kings in 2025 but has yet to make his NBA regular-season debut.

Thomas finished out his college career with USC as a graduate transfer in 2024-25. He first signed with the Sixers on a Summer League deal after going unselected in the 2025 draft.

The forward most recently averaged 12.5 points on 46.5 percent shooting in 36 regular-season games for the Sixers' G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats.

Teams not set to travel internationally during the preseason are set to begin training camp Sept. 29. The Sixers are then scheduled to open the season Oct. 20 with a road game against the defending champion New York Knicks.

articles.title: Thanasis Antetokounmpo Leaves NBA for Overseas Contract After Giannis' Bucks-Heat Trade
articles.summary: The Antetokounmpo brothers won't be together during the 2026-27 NBA season, as Thanasis is continuing his professional career in Greece.
articles.body:
The Antetokounmpo brothers won't be together during the 2026-27 NBA season, as Thanasis is continuing his professional career in Greece.

Aris B.C. of the Greek Basketball League announced on Tuesday that Thanasis Antetokounmpo has signed a two-year deal with the club that includes a team option for a third season.

Antetokounmpo, the older brother of Giannis, has played seven seasons in the NBA spread over 11 years. He came to the United States in 2013 when he was drafted by the Delaware 87ers of the then-NBA Developmental League, now known as the G League.

The following year, Antetokounmpo was drafted into the NBA by the New York Knicks with the No. 51 overall pick. He spent most of the next two seasons with their D-League club, but did get play back-to-back NBA games on Jan. 29 and 31, 2016.

Following the 2015-16 season, Antetokounmpo went to play overseas in Spain and Greece for three years. He returned to the NBA in July 2019 when the Milwaukee Bucks signed him, pairing him with Giannis.

Thanasis wound up playing seven seasons with the Bucks, winning an NBA title during the 2020-21 campaign. He missed the entire 2024-25 season due to a torn Achilles before returning in 2025-26.

The 34-year-old appeared in 34 games with the Bucks last season. He averaged 1.4 points off the bench. Giannis left the Bucks this offseason when he was traded to the Miami Heat.

Aris B.C. finished 14-10 during the 2025-26 regular season and made the playoffs. The Emperor lost in the quarterfinals to AEK.

articles.title: Totti contra Doncic: las dos nuevas caras del baloncesto que quieren conquistar Roma
articles.standfirst: El mítico exfutbolista, asesor y consejero del Máxima Roma, rival en la capital italiana del Roma Basketball, del Luka Doncic es accionista
articles.summary: El mítico exfutbolista, asesor y consejero del Máxima Roma, rival en la capital italiana del Roma Basketball de Luka Doncic
articles.body: El exfutbolista italiano Francesco Totti, leyenda del Roma, se convirtió este martes en asesor y consejero del Máxima Roma de baloncesto, un nuevo club en la capital italiana que disputará la Serie A y la Eurocup después de adquirir el título deportivo del Pallacanestro Brescia. "Tenía ganas de nuevos estímulos y sentía el deseo de ponerme a prueba aceptando un nuevo desafío. El rol y, sobre todo, el proyecto que me propusieron me convencieron desde el primer momento", dijo el romano en sus redes sociales, tras confirmar que también será el delegado para el desarrollo de la base de las aficiones y de las operaciones de RSC (Responsabilidad Social Corporativa). "La ambición es importante, pero lo es aún más el deseo de construir algo que pueda perdurar en el tiempo: queremos regalar a Roma y a los romanos un equipo de baloncesto al que apoyar, en el que reconocerse y del cual sentirse orgullosos", agregó. Totti se unió así al proyecto de Paul Matiasic, un inversor italo-estadounidense que compró el título deportivo del Brescia, equipo que militaba en la máxima categoría, y lo trasladó a Roma con vistas a la temporada 2026-2027 con aspiraciones de convertirse en referencia italiana y europea. La elección de Totti como consejero, según explicó el club, responde a su condición de "símbolo de Roma", además de representar "el alma romana y la ambición global" que definen el proyecto. El Maxima Roma tendrá que competir por la atención, la audiencia y la afición de la capital italiana con el Basketball Club Roma SPQR, otro club creado para esta nueva campaña y que cuenta con Luka Doncic como inversor y con Sergio Scariolo como asesor tras su salida del Real Madrid. La Serie A comienza el 27 de septiembre y apenas habrá que esperar tres jornadas para el primer derbi de la capital italiana entre ambos equipos, que se disputará el 11 de octubre. En la Eurocup, la segunda competición europea de clubes detrás de la Euroliga, ambos tendrán presencia; el Maxima Roma se enfrentará a Venezia, Cluj, Ankara, Tenerife, Siauliai, London Lions y Frankfurt, mientras que Basketball Club Roma SPQR competirá contra el Bahçeşehir, Panevezys, Botevgrad, Manresa, PAOK, Ulm y Bosna Sarajevo, que ocupa el lugar del Mónaco, según se informó hoy.

articles.title: El Baskonia se queda en cuadro: cancela su amistoso y pierde a Diop, rumbo a la NBA
articles.standfirst: Los vitorianos, sin jugadores para afrontar el partido de este miércoles ante el Gipuzkoa
articles.summary: Los vitorianos, sin jugadores para afrontar el partido de este miércoles ante el Gipuzkoa
articles.body: El Baskonia ha suspendido el amistoso que debía disputar este miércoles ante el Gipuzkoa Basket, en el que iba a estrenarse esta pretemporada. El motivo es que el conjunto vitoriano no dispone de jugadores suficientes para afrontar el encuentro, en un momento especialmente complicado por las ausencias que arrastra la plantilla. El partido estaba previsto a puerta cerrada y formaba parte del calendario de preparación anunciado por el club. Entre las bajas se encuentran Khalifa Diop, que ya está en Estados Unidos; Kobi Simmons y Damion Baugh, ambos concentrados con sus respectivas selecciones y que han obtenido recientemente pasaportes Cotonou, además de otras ausencias que han reducido al mínimo el grupo disponible. Kenneth Faried, último fichaje baskonista, también se incorporará próximamente al equipo. La acumulación de ausencias ha obligado finalmente al club a renunciar al primer test de la pretemporada. El caso más importante es el de Khalifa Diop, que puede estar viviendo sus últimas horas como jugador del Baskonia. El pívot senegalés, elegido por los Cleveland Cavaliers en el número 39 del Draft de 2022, ha viajado con permiso del club a Cleveland para someterse al reconocimiento médico. Si supera las pruebas, los Cavaliers decidirán si incorporarlo a su plantilla para la temporada 2026-27. La operación todavía no es oficial, pero el Baskonia ya se prepara para el escenario de su salida. Diop tiene contrato en vigor y, por tanto, su salto a la NBA exigiría una compensación económica al club vitoriano. Su marcha dejaría a Paolo Galbiati sin una de sus principales piezas interiores y obligaría al Baskonia a acelerar el mercado para incorporar dos jugadores para la pintura, después de la llegada de Kenneth Faried.

articles.title: Skylar Diggins Rips Sky for Lack of 'Resources,' Blames Injuries on Not Getting Practice Facility
articles.summary: It's safe to say Skylar Diggins' first season with the Chicago Sky did not go as planned after she joined the team this past offseason on a two-year deal.
articles.body:
It's safe to say Skylar Diggins' first season with the Chicago Sky did not go as planned after she joined the team this past offseason on a two-year deal.

The guard has not played since July 3 because of a right knee injury, and the team announced Tuesday she would miss the rest of the season. But for her part, Diggins placed some of the blame on the organization for its lack of "resources" for the players.

"We need resources," she said, per ESPN . "... I think leading the league in injuries is not coincidental."

Angel Reese breaks yet another WNBA record

Diggins, who was moved out of the starting lineup earlier this season and revealed she had been playing through knee pain at the time, also said, "I hadn't been feeling like myself out there. After we reevaluated, we just decided to scale back and shut it down for the season."

The Sky are expected to have a new practice facility by next year, and Diggins said she is "looking forward to it." However, she was also asked if knowing what was in store in terms of the lack of resources and a dedicated practice facility would have impacted her decision to join Chicago last offseason.

"That's hard to say," Diggins told reporters . "... I understand how those things go as far as delays ... I'll be looking forward to it next year ... We need resources ... and I think leading the league in injuries is not coincidental."

She continued and called the lack of a facility "the biggest frustration within the season, just never feeling like we had a home base."

Diggins is far from the only notable Sky player who dealt with injuries this season.

Rickea Jackson was lost for the year in the early going due to a torn ACL, while DiJonai Carrington has been sidelined multiple times. Carrington has played just 11 games this season.

Diggins seemed to be a major addition for a Sky team in rebuilding mode this past offseason with a resume that includes six All-WNBA selections, seven All-Star nods and a Most Improved Player.

She averaged 14.2 points, 4.9 assists and 3.2 rebounds in 19 games this season.

As for Chicago, it is 15-25 on the campaign and playing out the string after being eliminated from playoff contention. It is the fourth straight losing season for the franchise that still isn't that far removed from its 2021 title.

articles.title: Athletic directors pick a side in college sports' biggest fight
articles.summary: With a Senate vote approaching, FBS ADs endorsed the Protect College Sports Act, arguing it could bring order to a system increasingly shaped by chaos
articles.body:
Penning a letter of support directly obtained by USA TODAY Sports for the proposed Protect College Sports Act , the Football Bowl Subdivision Athletics Directors Association on Tuesday, Sept. 1, made its stance on the 171-page bill public.

Awaiting a floor vote when Senate resumes in mid-September, the PCSA boasts bi-partisan support - with initial co-sponsors from Sens. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) and Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) - and seeks to broad oversight regarding collegiate athletics, specifically as it pertains to transfer rules, when coaches can be fired/hired and potential expansion as well as guardrails on revenue-sharing and Name, Image and Likeness monies. It also includes a carve-out for potential extra financial investment into women's and Olympic, non-revenue sports.

"On behalf of the members of the Football Bowls Subdivision Athletics Directors Association, I write to express our strong support for the Protect College Sports Act of 2026," the letter, attributed to FBS Executive Athletics Directors Association head Dan Radakovich, read, "and to thank you for your leadership in advancing legislation to address some of the most significant challenges faces college athletics."

A former athletics director at Clemson who stepped down from his post at Miami (Fla.) on June 1, 2026, Radakovich's letter further outlined the collective stance of A.D.s at the top level of college football.

"As athletics directors, our members are responsible for putting college sports policy into practice every day, supporting student-athletes, supervising coaches and compliance staffs, managing rosters and resources, and planning for the long-term success of broad-based athletics programs," Radakovich wrote. "We believe this legislation addresses the issues where congressional action is most needed.

"Our members feel the impacts of today's fragmented legal and regulatory environment firsthand. The current system has contributed to annual roster turnover, inconsistent eligibility guidance, unregulated agent activity, recruiting inducements, and school-connected spending routed through third parties to circumvent a common compensation framework."

See who made college football US LBM Coaches Poll preseason top 25

USA TODAY Sports reported extensively Tuesday, Aug. 25, about the arrival of the $50 million roster this season in college football and that literally dozens of FBS head coaches, general managers and agents in the NIL space tabbed at least 11 programs with roster spends around or above $40 million.

"For our members, the need is straightforward: student-athletes should have clear rights and protection," Radakovich's letter continued. "Institutions should compete under common and enforceable rules, and athletics departments should be able to make long-term decisions with greater certainty."

NCAA moves toward allowing joint football practices

Perhaps most notably, Colorado coach Deion Sanders and Syracuse coach Fran Brown sought to have their respective FBS teams host joint spring football practices.

The NCAA, back in 2025, was not ready to adopt or allow such a proposal on the fly.

Now, however, college athletics' governing body is a step closer to allowing joint practices between two four-year institutions - at the Football Championship Subdivision level.

The NCAA noted the first hurdle was cleared in procedures conducted Monday, Aug. 31.

Per the NCAA's release , "FCS Programs would be able to engage in a joint practice with another four-year school during the spring academic term."

The NCAA also noted that it had advanced a proposal to allow the preseason practice period at the FCS level to include up to 21 practices in a 27-day span.

The notification of transfer period also would shrink from 15 days to 10, beginning with the first business day of the 2027 year, which would be Jan. 4, 2027, for the coming period.

The Division I Cabinet will meet Oct. 6-7, 2026, to vote on these potential policy changes, as well as other items at the FBS level.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Reacts to 'King of New York' Nickname After Knicks' 2026 NBA Title Win
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson isn't embracing the moniker recently bestowed upon him by Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson isn't embracing the moniker recently bestowed upon him by Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Mamdani dubbed Brunson the "king" of New York City after he played an instrumental role in the Knicks' championship run.

The three-time All-Star discussed the nickname on the newest episode of the Road Trippin' Show . He said he has "never called myself the 'King of New York'" and "will never call myself the 'King of New York.'"

Brunson can't stop others from calling him the king of the Big Apple, but it's easy to see why he'd want to distance himself from that distinction. That would be quite the crown to wear.

The Knicks aren't going to win every single NBA title between now and when Brunson eventually retires. Even if the franchise's fortunes take a turn, it may do little to dampen the general goodwill toward the guard.

Eli Manning's popularity with New York Giants fans endured even as his performance declined and the team struggled to contend. The same was true for New York Yankees legend Derek Jeter.

For Brunson, the 2026 Finals probably made him New York royalty in perpetuity.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Reveals Knicks' Mindset in New Video After Winning 2026 NBA Title
articles.summary: New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson detailed the team's mindset moving forward after winning the 2026 NBA Finals.
articles.body:
New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson detailed the team's mindset moving forward after winning the 2026 NBA Finals.

"We don't want to speak of the trophy, we don't want to talk about the trophy, we don't want to see the trophy," Brunson said during a Tuesday appearance on the Road Trippin' Show . "We want to come in with the same mindset if not even tougher mindset we had last year."

The Knicks used a "0-0" mentality throughout their 2026 playoff run, entering every postseason game as if it were the beginning of the series without paying attention to whether they were leading or trailing.

The approach worked, as New York went 16-3 in the playoffs before ending the organization's 53-year championship drought. The Knicks outscored their opponents by 283 points in the postseason, representing the greatest playoff point differential in NBA history .

Brunson was stellar throughout New York's postseason run, ranking No. 1 in the NBA by averaging 28.4 points per game in the playoffs.

He also earned Finals MVP honors by averaging 32.6 points, 4.6 assists and 2.0 steals per game on 42.1/38.9/86.0 shooting splits during the team's five-game series victory over the San Antonio Spurs to capture the Larry O'Brien Trophy.

As the Knicks prepare to enter the 2026-27 season as defending champions, they won't be dwelling on their recent title.

articles.summary: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry's knee will need to be managed moving forward after he was plagued by health issues during the 2025-26 season, according to Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry's knee will need to be managed moving forward after he was plagued by health issues during the 2025-26 season, according to Monte Poole of NBC Sports Bay Area.

"There's at least some lingering concern about the knee," Poole reported Tuesday on the Dubs Talk podcast. "From what I've been told, it can be managed, but it has to be managed and that's a new thing for Steph because people always say he's the most conditioned guy in the league and now he has to manage a knee. I guess we'll find out but from what I understand, he and his trainers have devised ways to kind of work around that and sort of support that whole possibility of the knee not being as great as he wants it to be. So, I'm curious to see how it turns out, but Steph seemed pretty confident that he'll be able to go out there and put out 70+ games."

Curry was limited to just 43 appearances last season while dealing with patellofemoral pain syndrome , which is also known as "runner's knee."

The two-time MVP initially experienced pain and swelling in his right knee during a workout in Minneapolis on Jan. 24 (h/t ESPN's Anthony Slater ). He played through the knee issues before he eventually left Golden State's lineup on Jan. 30.

Curry was sidelined for over two months while he recovered, finally making his return on April 5.

He played in four of of the Warriors' final five regular-season games and was on the floor for both of their play-in tournament contests. Golden State ultimately missed the playoffs with a 37-45 record.

Curry confirmed that the knee injury changed his offseason regimen.

"Yeah, it's just a more patient approach," Curry told Poole in July. "Quality over quantity, (with) the idea that I can still get to the level that I need to."

"Just being a little bit more mindful of how to balance a four-month summer," he added. "Knowing that I need the rest, but I also don't want to get too far away where it's hard to get back. So, it's just being more mindful with timing and spacing throughout the summer."

While the Warriors could be cautious with Curry's availability next season, he seems to be targeting at least 70 games played.

The 12-time All-Star is expected to shoulder a heavy offensive burden during his 2026-27 campaign, as Golden State has put together a relatively quiet offseason.

The Warriors primarily focused on bringing back their own free agents including Draymond Green, Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford, De'Anthony Melton and Gary Payton II. They were reportedly interested in signing LeBron James before he became a member of the Philadelphia 76ers.

Despite Curry's knee issues, he remained impactful when healthy last season.

He averaged 26.6 points, 4.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game while shooting 46.8 percent from the field and 39.3 percent from three-point territory.

articles.title: NBA roster update: Philadelphia 76ers bring in 7-foot-6 star to support LeBron James’ championship dream
articles.summary: NBA News: Tacko Fall is heading back to the NBA. The 7-foot-6 center has signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, giving him a shot to earn a rost.
articles.body: Tacko Fall is heading back to the NBA. The 7-foot-6 center has signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the Philadelphia 76ers, giving him a shot to earn a roster spot when training camp opens in New Jersey later this month.It's a modest move on paper, but it lands during arguably the busiest offseason in franchise history, one that already brought in LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. And if Fall sticks around past camp, sharing a locker room with James would be one of the more unexpected subplots of his NBA return.Philadelphia 76ers sign Tacko Fall and two other starsTacko Fall, 30, hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season with Cleveland. Across parts of three seasons with the Celtics and Cavaliers, he appeared in 37 games and averaged 2.2 points, 2.4 rebounds and 6.2 minutes. Since then, he's played overseas, most recently with the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association, and he spent last season with the New Zealand Breakers, averaging 11.4 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.6 blocks over 18 games.He isn't arriving alone. Guard Jameer Nelson Jr. and forward Saint Thomas also signed Exhibit 10 contracts, with terms undisclosed. The team confirmed the moves directly: "We have signed Tacko Fall, Jameer Nelson Jr., and Saint Thomas," the Sixers posted on X.Nelson, 25, averaged 18.9 points and 3.4 assists last season with the G League's Stockton Kings. He's the son of longtime NBA guard Jameer Nelson, who now serves as the Sixers' executive vice president of basketball operations. Thomas, 23, spent last season with Philadelphia's G League affiliate, the Delaware Blue Coats, putting up 12.5 points and 5.0 rebounds a game before appearing in four Summer League contests for the Sixers this year.Why Philadelphia made the moveNone of the three is likely to make a real dent in the rotation, and making the roster at all is far from guaranteed. Philadelphia enters camp with Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, Brown and James all on the roster, and questions about outside shooting, defensive versatility and health, particularly around Embiid and a 41-year-old James, haven't gone away. Head coach Nick Nurse will be the one tasked with making the fit work. The Sixers open their regular season on October 20 against the Knicks.LeBron James is serious about a Philadelphia 76ers championshipJames is entering his 24th NBA season, his first with the Sixers after eight years with the Lakers that included a championship in 2020. He's said the chance to compete for another title, not money, is what pulled him to Philadelphia.On August 31, he posted an Instagram story of himself shirtless and sweating through a workout, writing "It's just WORK!!" before flashing a goofy grin at the camera. It's a familiar move for James, who's built a career partly on showing his offseason grind, and the clip spread quickly online.He's already logging time with new teammates. Brown described a recent session in Los Angeles with James and Maxey under trainer Chris Johnson during a Twitch stream: "I've been working, building chemistry with the guys." He added that the energy and talent in the room were obvious, though he was careful not to get ahead of himself about what it all means once the season starts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pair of ex-Warriors front-office employees file lawsuit alleging gender, age and racial discrimination
articles.summary: Two former Warriors front office employees alleged that they suffered "humiliation, emotional distress, embarrassment and mental and physical pain and anguis...
articles.body:
A pair of former Golden State Warriors employees filed a lawsuit against the organization after losing their jobs.

The two women filed the lawsuit in San Francisco County Superior Court last week, according to The Athletic's Devon Henderson , and are alleging gender, age and race-based discrimination, workplace harassment and retaliation.

Lisa Shelley worked as the Warriors' associate general counsel and their director of business and legal affairs and risk management. Jennifer Vasquez was the team's vice president of diversity, equity and inclusion. The two said they suffered "humiliation, emotional distress, embarrassment and mental and physical pain and anguish" during their time working for the Warriors' front office. The workplace, they said in the lawsuit, was "marked by discrimination, hostility and retaliation."

Shelley was hired by the Warriors in 2021, and she claims the team passed her over for multiple promotions and at one point promoted a younger male employee with less experience over her. According to The Athletic, she secured corporate partnerships worth more than $4 million during her time with the Warriors, among other things, and was also once named employee of the month.

Shelley was fired in December 2025, when she was told the team's legal department was being "reimagined." She alleged in the lawsuit that her superior was not present in the termination meeting, either, which is against team policy.

Then, less than two weeks later, Vasquez was fired after the Warriors opted to eliminate their DEI function. Vasquez declined to characterize her departure as "voluntary" like the team requested, and she was fired in January.

Both Shelley and Vasquez criticized the team's workplace culture for women, and said that the team's chief people officer, Erin Dangerfield, "regularly criticized female employees' bodies, physical appearance, and wardrobe choices." Women of color or with larger body types, per the report, were disproportionately targeted.

"Early in Plaintiff Vasquez's employment, during a one-on-one meeting, Dangerfield told Plaintiff Vasquez that women who wanted to work in professional sports often did so because they were 'jersey chasers,' referring to women who sought employment in sports to pursue romantic or sexual attention from professional athletes," the lawsuit reads, per the report.

Vasquez alleged that she was once laughed at for being over 40 years old in a team meeting, and was told she had to "play the game" to succeed despite others sharing in similar discomforts.

Shelley also claimed that she lost a job offer from the Los Angeles Clippers earlier this year after the Warriors "made false and disparaging statements" when contacted for a reference. A conditional offer of employment that she had received in June was withdrawn, per the report.

"Plaintiffs were drawn to the GSW, in part, because San Francisco is one of the most culturally diverse cities in the country, and a national bastion for human rights," the lawsuit reads. "The culturally responsible, family-oriented environment that Plaintiffs Vasquez and Shelley expected when they joined GSW was far from what they endured."

The Clippers declined to comment to The Athletic on Tuesday, while the Warriors denied the allegations made against them.

"Golden State prides itself on its commitment to maintaining an inclusive environment grounded in mutual respect and professionalism," the Warriors said in a statement. "We take all workplace concerns seriously. The lawsuit filed by two former employees contains allegations that are false, misleading, and unsupported by credible evidence. Many of the allegations have been previously reviewed or investigated and found to be without merit. "Golden State intends to vigorously defend against these baseless claims and is confident that an examination of the facts will confirm that Golden State, its leadership, and the employees targeted in this lawsuit have at all times operated with the highest levels of integrity and fairness."

articles.title: El Dream Team femenino pone a prueba su aplastante dominio: 69-0 desde 2006, pero ¿puede perder?
articles.standfirst: El crecimiento de los rivales, la ajustada final olímpica de los Juegos de París (67-66), las importantes bajas y la falta de preparación abren la puerta a la campanada
articles.summary: El crecimiento de los rivales, la ajustada final olímpica de los Juegos de París (67-66), las importantes bajas y la falta de preparación abren la puerta a la campanada
articles.body: Desde que los Juegos de Barcelona en 1992 vieron el nacimiento del irrepetible Dream Team, muchos combinados masculinos de Estados Unidos han llevado ese sobrenombre tanto si se acercaban a la versión original como si no. En cambio, el término sí ha hecho justicia a las selecciones femeninas, cuyo dominio ha sido abrumador en torneos a nivel planetario. En los Juegos Olímpicos, las estadounidenses no pierden un partido desde la semifinal de, precisamente, Barcelona'92, cuando cayeron por 73-79 ante el Equipo Unificado en plena desintegración de la Unión Soviética. Después ganarían el duelo por el bronce, iniciando una racha que se ha traducido en un balance de 61-0 y ocho oros consecutivos. En los Mundiales han estado en todos los podios desde 1979 ganando nueve de ellos y los últimos cuatro de manera consecutiva. Su última derrota en el torneo data del 21 de septiembre de 2006, cuando cedió en semifinales contra Rusia (75-68). Como vencieron en la lucha por la tercera plaza, 33-0 desde entonces. Y el último título, hace cuatro años se lo llevaron con una diferencia media de 40,75 puntos en sus ocho triunfos. Sumando las dos competiciones, el balance desde su último tropiezo es de 69-0 con una recompensa de cinco oros olímpicos y cuatro mundiales. Ninguna otra selección de ningún país o disciplina ha ejercido un dominio tan bestial como las jugadoras estadounidenses de baloncesto. Ahora aspira a mantenerlo con un equipo plagado de grandes nombres: Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper... y jóvenes como Aliyah Boston, Paige Bueckers, Angel Reese y la mediática Caitlin Clark, que se estrenará en un gran torneo internacional. Y, sin embargo, ¿se ve Estados Unidos amenazada en este Mundial que está a punto de arrancar? La final olímpica de París fue todo un aviso. Las anfitrionas estuvieron cerca de dar una campanada histórica. Perdieron por 67-66 tras llevar al límite a la selección invencible. "Francia estuvo muy cerca y eso debería servirnos de advertencia. Debemos asegurarnos de estar preparadas cada partido, sin desmerecer a nadie. Aquel día ellas jugaron muy bien, pero creo que no fue nuestra mejor actuación y queremos dar lo mejor de nosotras", asegura Breanna Stewart, estrella del combinado actual y una de las mejores jugadoras de la historia. Francia parte como una de las principales amenazas para el combinado norteamericano. Las galas tienen 12 jugadoras en la WNBA y cinco de ellas han sido incluidas en una lista con las 50 mejores de la competición. Ocho estarán en el Mundial. Por físico, ellas y Australia no andan lejos de Estados Unidos. "Todos los equipos y todos los países están mejorando. En Estados Unidos, debemos seguir elevando nuestro nivel de juego", considera Stewart. Lo extraño de la preparación también alimenta la posibilidad de ver una campanada. La WNBA se ha detenido hace unos pocos días, con lo que las internacionales estadounidenses apenas han tenido oportunidad de entrenarse juntas ni han disputado ningún amistoso. Además, este lunes se conocían las importantes ausencias por problemas físicos de A'ja Wilson y Kelsey Plum. La primera, probablemente la jugadora más dominante del mundo con cuatro MVP de la WNBA, era el referente interior. La segunda iba a ser una de las brújulas en el puesto de base. La selección femenina de Estados Unidos, el equipo que nunca pierde, parece más amenazado que nunca en la historia reciente. El Mundial se presenta como una exigente prueba para su aplastante dominio.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown reacts to another ex-Celtic joining Sixers
articles.summary: Former Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown may have worked some recruiting magic to get Tacko Fall, another former Celtic, to the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
NBA friendships are a funny thing. Star players don't only hang out with other star players. They often become close with bench warmers who have a completely different role on the team. At least, that seems to be the case with former Boston Celtics star Jaylen Brown and former Celtics bench warmer Tacko Fall.

The unlikely duo played together for two years in Boston during the 2019-20 and 2020-21 seasons. Fall entered just 26 games with the Celtics and still managed to emerge as a fan favorite thanks to his incredible 7-foot-6 stature and kind nature. Around that same time, Brown helped lead the C's on the court while befriending Fall off the court. Despite the fact that they didn't share the floor much, they made such a lasting bond that Brown is the godfather to Fall's daughter. The two were even seen hanging out in Morocco in late June.

Shortly after Brown and Fall spent time in northern Africa, the former was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in a shocking blockbuster deal. This move ended up creating a Celtics reunion, as the latter signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Sixers and plans to participate in training camp at the end of September.

Fall, who hasn't played in an NBA game since 2022, will look to earn a more permanent role with the Sixers organization. Brown was happy to see his friend land a camp deal with his current squad and took to X (formerly known as Twitter) to celebrate:

Whether or not one of the tallest players in NBA history can stay in the Association remains to be seen. However, he's getting a shot, and perhaps Brown played a role in that.

The rival 76ers now roster three former Celtics, including Brown, Fall, and shooting guard Anfernee Simons. If they all stick around, the first time they'll see the Green Team during the 2026-27 campaign would be in a preseason matchup that takes place on Saturday, October 10 in Boston.

articles.title: New Additions Tacko Fall And Dean Wade Speak On Joining The 76ers
articles.summary: The 76ers' new additions, Tacko Fall and Dean Wade, make their feelings known on joining the franchise in Philadelphia.
articles.body:
Tacko Fall , the seven foot six inch tall forward, has signed an Exhibit-10 deal to return to the NBA with the Philadelphia 76ers after a four-year absence from the league .

Following the announcement, Fall spoke to Brandon 'Scoop B' Robinson and shared his emotions about potentially returning to the NBA and reuniting with his former Boston Celtics teammate, Jaylen Brown , in Philadelphia.

"It is an opportunity of a lifetime that I shall not waste," Fall told Robinson. "Really looking forward to playing alongside JB and doing whatever it takes to help the team."

Fall last played for the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2022, where he came off the bench in 11 games and averaged 2.1 rebounds, 1.1 points, and 0.5 blocks while shooting 41.7% from the field. He was a teammate of Jaylen Brown for two seasons on the Boston Celtics.

Fall actually played professionally abroad rather than disappearing from the league. He played for the New Zealand Breakers in Australia's NBL after spending significant time in China, including with the Jiangsu Flying Tigers and Nanjing Monkey Kings.

Later on, he joined the Ningbo Rockets in the Chinese Basketball Association. Fall continued to use his enormous size as a finisher and rim protector, averaging 11.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 2.2 blocks per game most recently.

Fall also tested an alternative career path , training to become a firefighter in Chicago to give back to the community before returning to basketball.

The 2026 NBA All-Star Celebrity Game gave American fans another chance to see Fall. With 20 points, 21 rebounds, and five blocks, he dominated the competition and demonstrated how challenging it can be to deal with his size around the hoop.

Alongside Tacko Fall, the 76ers have also given Exhibit-10 deals to Jameer Nelson Jr. and Saint Thomas. All three players are eligible for two-way deals, and the 76ers also have one roster spot open for a standard contract.

Weeks before these additions, the 76ers also strengthened their frontcourt by signing another former Cavaliers player, Dean Wade , on a four-year, $38.7 million deal. Wade spoke to Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints and expressed his feelings about joining the 76ers with a bold statement.

"Trying to be as unbiased as I can, when I look at this team, it's hard to ignore the talent. It stands out immediately. This is by far the best team I've ever been on, and that's not to talk down about any other team I've been a part of."

"We had some really great teams in Cleveland with some very talented players, but this team in Philadelphia now is a step above. We are the real deal when it comes to truly being in the championship mix. There is no doubt in my mind that this team has what it takes to compete for a championship, and it seems like the media shares that mindset right now," Wade told Siegel.

Dean Wade ended the 2025-26 season averaging 5.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.3 assists in 77 games played across the regular season and playoffs combined. He shot 44.3% from the field and 36.5% from the three-point line.

Wade is coming off an Eastern Conference Finals run with the Cavaliers, and yet he feels this team has better prospects than his former team. Both players seem extremely confident and highly motivated coming into the season.

While it is still unclear whether Tacko Fall will be on the roster when the regular season starts, his Exhibit-10 deal makes training camp a promising opportunity to earn an NBA contract with the 76ers.

Even though most eyes are on the starting lineup, bench depth often makes a team a championship contender. Hence, it will be interesting to see how Dean Wade and potentially Tacko Fall can contribute to the 76ers' championship ambitions in 2026-27.
